scenes.text: Your dollar is named after a deer.
scenes.say: [amused] Your dollar is named after a deer.
scenes.head: YOUR DOLLAR IS NAMED AFTER A DEER

scenes.text: 1748. A trader slides a barrel across the counter.
scenes.say: [storytelling] Seventeen forty-eight. A trader slides a barrel across the counter.

scenes.text: Five skins. Take it or leave it.
scenes.say: [gruff] Five skins. Take it or leave it.

scenes.text: Not coins. Not paper. Deer skins.
scenes.say: [amused] Not coins. Not paper. Deer skins.

scenes.text: Out here, nobody had money. But everybody had deer.
scenes.say: Out here, nobody had money. But everybody had deer.

scenes.text: One good skin bought you a knife. Five bought you a barrel.
scenes.say: [matter-of-fact] One good skin bought you a knife. Five bought you a barrel.

scenes.text: Then a man writes in his journal that he was robbed... of 300 bucks.
scenes.say: [dramatic] Then a man writes in his journal that he was robbed... of three hundred bucks.

scenes.text: Not dollars. The U.S. dollar didn't exist yet.
scenes.say: [whispers] Not dollars. The U.S. dollar didn't exist yet.

scenes.text: It showed up 44 years later. In 1792.
scenes.say: It showed up forty-four years later. In seventeen ninety-two.
scenes.show_source: Coinage Act of 1792 created the U.S. dollar

scenes.text: By then, people already had a word for 'one unit of stuff you trade.'
scenes.say: By then, people already had a word for 'one unit of stuff you trade.'

scenes.text: So that's probably why your dollar is a buck. Historians still argue about it.
scenes.say: [thoughtful] So that's probably why your dollar is a buck. Historians still argue about it.

scenes.text: Me? I just like the name.
scenes.say: [smug] Me? I just like the name.
